draft.title: What an entrepreneur does
card: An entrepreneur starts a new business, or grows one, in the hope of making a profit. They bring resources together to make something new or better.
Spots an opportunity
notices a need or want that people would pay to have met, such as no café near a busy beach.
Takes a risk
puts in money, time or effort without knowing if the business will work. If it fails, they can lose what they put in.
Organises resources
brings together what the business needs, such as equipment, materials and workers, and puts them to use.
draft.remember: An entrepreneur sees a chance, risks something to chase it, and gathers what the business needs.

a.q: Ana wants to be an entrepreneur. Which of these choices fits?
opts: Ana uses her savings to start a dog-washing van business
Ana earns a wage washing dogs at a pet shop
Ana pays a business to wash her dog each month
Ana writes a review of a dog-washing van
a.why: Ana risks her own savings to start a business, so she is acting as an entrepreneur. Working for a wage is tempting, but the pet shop's owner carries the risk, not Ana.
a.clue: Who could lose money if the business fails?

b.q: Hamid sees that cyclists in his town travel an hour to get bikes fixed. He asks friends if they would pay for repairs closer to home. He has spent nothing yet. Which part of being an entrepreneur is this?
opts: Spotting an opportunity
Taking a financial risk
Organising his resources
Making a profit from sales
b.why: Hamid has found a need that people would pay to have met, which is spotting an opportunity. He has not put in any money yet, so he is not taking a risk.
b.clue: He has noticed something, but he has not spent anything.

a.best: Ana uses her savings to start a dog-washing van business

problems.detail: The why says Hamid is not taking a risk because he has put in no money. The card defines risk as putting in money, time or effort, and Hamid is spending some time and effort asking friends. The why should say he has not yet put anything at stake in a business, rather than tie risk only to money.
